events.content: NVIDIA Data Center revenue Q3 fiscal 2027 ended October 2025

NVIDIA has not yet reported Data Center revenue for Q3 fiscal 2027 (the quarter ending in October 2026); its Q3 FY2027 earnings release is scheduled for November 17, 2026. [[1]] 

The latest reported Data Center revenue is **$89.0 billion** for Q2 fiscal 2027, reported on August 26, 2026. [[2]] 

For Q3 FY2027, NVIDIA guided only total company revenue to **$108.0 billion, plus or minus 2%**, and stated that it assumed no China Data Center compute revenue in that outlook; it did not provide a standalone Data Center-revenue forecast. [[2]]

events.content: NVIDIA Data Center revenue growth drivers Q2 fiscal 2027 fiscal results August 2026

**NVIDIA Data Center revenue in Q2 FY2027:** Revenue was **$89.0 billion**, up **18% sequentially** and **117% year over year**, in the quarter ended July 26, 2026. [[1]]

**Primary growth drivers**

- **Sustained Blackwell demand at hyperscalers:** Hyperscale revenue reached **$49 billion**, rising **13% quarter over quarter**, driven by continued Blackwell strength as additional GPU capacity entered service. [[2]]
- **Faster growth from AI-cloud, enterprise, industrial and sovereign customers:** The ACIE segment—neocloud, industrial and enterprise customers—generated **$40 billion**, increasing **25% sequentially** and **138% year over year**. [[2]]
- **Neocloud capacity expansion:** ACIE growth reflected new neocloud capacity built to serve enterprise customers, AI startups and sovereign-AI users, while hyperscalers also bought neocloud capacity to supplement their internal data-center construction. [[2]]
- **Broad-based AI-infrastructure buildout:** NVIDIA characterized demand as spanning hyperscalers, AI labs, AI-native companies, enterprises and sovereign customers, rather than depending on one customer group. [[2]]
- **Customer capex and cloud backlog:** NVIDIA cited cloud-industry backlog above **$2 trillion** and projected top-five-hyperscaler capex of nearly **$800 billion in 2026** and **$1.3 trillion in 2027**, supporting continued purchases of AI compute infrastructure. [[2]]
- **Platform content expansion:** NVIDIA said its full-stack AI-factory architecture expands its revenue opportunity per gigawatt from roughly **$18 billion with Hopper** to **$25 billion with Blackwell** and **$40 billion with Vera Rubin**, reflecting higher system-level content across GPUs, CPUs, NVLink, networking, systems and software. [[2]]
- **Strong utilization and constrained supply:** NVIDIA reported that its compute capacity was fully utilized across the clouds it serves and described its FY2028 outlook as supply constrained, indicating demand exceeded immediately available supply. [[2]]

**Analytical takeaway:** Q2’s Data Center growth was driven by both a large hyperscale Blackwell deployment cycle and a faster-growing second engine—AI-cloud, enterprise and sovereign demand—making the $89 billion result more diversified than a hyperscaler-only ramp. [[2]]

**Key caveat:** NVIDIA’s subsequent-quarter outlook of **$108.0 billion** in total company revenue assumed **no Data Center compute revenue from China**, so the reported Q2 strength and forward outlook were  …[truncated]
